title: A Touch of Mercy: The First Bridge of Love to Your Child's Heart
summary:
Imagine your little one, eyes sparkling with curiosity, reaching out for a warm hug. In that simple, seemingly ordinary moment, bridges of love and security are built. These tender touches, shared smiles, and gentle whispers are not just expressions of affection; they are a strong foundation that connects your child to the world around them, giving them a deep sense of acceptance and comfort.

These warm feelings, with which you envelop your child, are the first building block in their understanding of religion. When your child connects love and security with your presence, and with the mercy Allah has placed in parents' hearts, it is hoped they will grow up upon a sound fitrah inclined toward faith in Allah. The Prophet ﷺ was an example in this; he kissed children, carried them, and showed them mercy, teaching us that mercy is the basis of dealing with creation, saying: «Whoever does not show mercy will not be shown mercy.» (Sahih al-Bukhari 5997). This mercy is the first lesson of faith your child receives.

Don't worry about searching for complex ways to instill faith. It is enough to give your child lots of love, hugs, and tender touches. Make every touch and every hug an implicit message that Allah is Merciful and Most Loving, and that His religion holds mercy and goodness. These simple actions contribute to shaping their awareness and planting seeds of faith in their heart, helping them see religion as a source of security and tranquility, rather than anxiety or aversion.
try_this: Tonight: Before your child sleeps, hug them tenderly for a full minute, and whisper warm words of your love for them in their ear.
reflection_prompts: How do I show my child that mercy is an essential part of my faith?
What are the moments when I feel I am giving my child unconditional love?
parent_script: «My darling, I love you very much, and this love is a gift from Allah to us.»
